notes: Method: every author list, year and arXiv id in each answer was checked against data/papers.json; relevance was judged from abstracts only. Cross-cutting points for the orchestrator: (1) Tool RESULTS are not stored in either jsonl, only tool CALLS, so citation counts (e.g. S5 q5's 6294 for Toolformer) and search-hit lists can only be judged by whether a matching call exists, not by their returned values. (2) CLIP (2103.00020) was treated consistently as 'borderline' for q8 in both systems: its abstract is plainly computer vision but never mentions transformers; the eval's own rationale lists it as a match. Both q8 verdicts flip from success to score 3 if borderline is counted as off-topic. (3) Under the corrected tool list, S4's statements that it lacked citation data (q2, q3, q9, q10) were treated as true and not penalised as errors; those four items score 2 purely because the rubric assigns 2 to 'most parts missing', so an honest tool-bound non-answer and a fabricating answer land on the same number -- the parts_done and factual_errors fields distinguish them. (4) The one genuine S4 factual error outside q5 is q9's 'The paper is not authored by Yao' (Yao is the last author of Reflexion). (5) S4 q5 is the only item scored 1: its ReAct BibTeX carries an invented author list. (6) S4 q8 produced correct BibTeX without format_citation (provenance gap, content right); S5 q8 used the tool but padded the list with BERT under a hedge -- both scored 4 for different reasons. (7) S5 q5 is scored 3 only because the found papers were never listed; under a lenient reading of 'find papers' it is a 4.
